text:
The Kebbi State Government, through the Agro-Climatic Resilience in Semi-Arid Landscapes (ACReSAL) project, has commenced an erosion control project in Badariya and Dukku Mallah communities in Birnin Kebbi Local Government Area.
Governor Nasir Idris flagged off the multi-million-naira project on Wednesday, describing it as a major intervention to address persistent erosion threatening lives, property and farmlands in the affected communities.
The governor expressed confidence that the project, upon completion, would provide a lasting solution to the erosion problem while improving the environmental outlook of Birnin Kebbi, the state capital.
Idris said that although the project was not among his campaign promises, his administration considered it necessary because of its importance to the safety, welfare and economic wellbeing of residents.
He explained that the intervention was being implemented under ACReSAL, a World Bank-assisted programme designed to tackle environmental degradation and strengthen resilience in vulnerable landscapes.
“The successful completion of this project will significantly reduce erosion problems in the affected communities, protect farmlands and create a more conducive environment for agricultural activities,” the governor said.
Idris also expressed confidence in the contractor handling the project, describing the company as a reputable multinational firm with specialised experience in erosion control.
“I have confidence in the company handling this project because of its specialisation in erosion control. My administration is determined to rescue the people of Dukku Mallah and Badariya from the persistent challenges posed by erosion,” he said.
The governor assured residents that his administration would ensure effective supervision and monitoring of the project to guarantee compliance with approved specifications and quality standards, as well as timely completion.
He reiterated his commitment to executing people-oriented projects that address pressing community needs, improve living conditions and stimulate economic activities across the state.
Idris urged residents of the benefiting communities to cooperate with the contractor and relevant project officials, adding that they should take collective responsibility for protecting and maintaining the infrastructure after completion.
Residents of the affected communities, who attended the flag-off ceremony in large numbers, commended the governor for the intervention, describing it as timely relief from the persistent threat erosion posed to their homes, farmlands and livelihoods.
